title: Yo Yo Honey Singh records statement in alleged obscene remarks case, questioned for over two hours: Reports
raw_summary:
Rapper and singer Yo Yo Honey Singh appeared before the Maharashtra Cyber Cell on Friday, October 16, and was questioned for more than two hours in connection with a complaint over his alleged objectionable remarks at a concert in Delhi in January 2026. The 43-year-old singer was summoned after a Mumbai resident filed a complaint regarding the remarks, following which the Maharashtra Cyber police registered a case and initiated an investigation.

Reportedly, the information shared by the Cyber Cell, Honey Singh had been summoned three times earlier but did not appear, citing his presence abroad. The authorities subsequently issued another summons directing him to appear on October 16. A senior Cyber Cell official had also warned that the process to issue a Look Out Circular (LOC) could be initiated if he failed to comply with the latest summons.

Honey Singh appeared before the investigating officers on Friday and was questioned for over two hours, according to sources. He left the premises after the questioning without responding to questions from the media. Why was Honey Singh summoned by the Maharashtra Cyber Cell? The case relates to alleged obscene remarks made by Honey Singh during a concert in Delhi in January 2026. A video clip from the performance later circulated on social media and drew criticism from several users.

According to earlier reports, the remarks allegedly included an indecent reference to having sex in cars. Following the online backlash, a Mumbai resident approached the cyber police with a complaint, leading to the registration of a case.

Honey Singh subsequently issued a video apology, acknowledging that his choice of words had offended people. Explaining his intention behind the remarks, he said, "Seeing a larger number of Gen Z, I tried to convey a message in a language which they would prefer. However, I deeply regret that the way I expressed this message was inappropriate and not acceptable to many. I offer my heartfelt apologies."

title: BMC demolishes parts of Ajay Devgn’s Juhu bungalow over alleged unauthorised construction: Reports
raw_summary:
The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has demolished parts of actor Ajay Devgn’s bungalow in Mumbai’s Juhu area following allegations of unauthorised construction. The civic action comes days after the municipal body issued a stop-work notice concerning structural alterations at the property.

Devgn’s 7,802-square-foot bungalow is located within the Kapole Co-operative Housing Society in Juhu. According to the BMC, construction-related work was being carried out at the property without the required municipal permissions. BMC issues stop-work notice The civic body said the work included internal alterations, the erection of partition walls, modifications to windows and other structural changes. The BMC subsequently issued a notice on September 10 under Section 354A of the Mumbai Municipal Corporation Act.

The notice directed that the work be stopped immediately and called for the submission of the necessary documents and permissions related to the construction.

According to the civic body, the construction activity continued despite the notice. BMC officials subsequently visited the property and took action against the portions of the structure that it deemed unauthorised.

Visuals from the spot showed civic officials using a hammer to dismantle parts of the construction. Ajay Devgn’s Drishyam 3 continues its theatrical run The civic action comes as Ajay Devgn’s latest release, Drishyam 3, continues its run in theatres. The third and final instalment of the crime thriller franchise was released on October 2 and has reportedly crossed the Rs 400 crore mark at the global box office.

Directed by Abhishek Pathak, the film also stars Shriya Saran, Tabu and Akshaye Khanna. Drishyam 3 has received largely positive reviews, with its performances, suspense and twists drawing attention from critics and audiences.

The film marks the latest chapter in the franchise, which follows Vijay Salgaonkar and his family as they attempt to deal with the consequences of a crime and the investigation surrounding it.

title: Neha Sharma warns against unauthorised AI content using her likeness: “I will take legal action”
raw_summary:
Actress Neha Sharma has issued a strong warning against the unauthorised use of her face and likeness in AI-generated videos and images. On October 17, the actor took to social media to ask people creating or circulating such content to remove it immediately and refrain from using her identity without consent.

In her post, Neha wrote, “Anyone using my face or likeness to create AI-generated videos or images without my consent is hereby warned to STOP IMMEDIATELY.”

She further asked for any such content already posted online to be taken down. “Take down all such content already posted and refrain from creating, editing, or circulating any further AI-generated videos or images using my identity. Using my face in this manner to misrepresent me or malign my reputation is completely unacceptable.” Neha Sharma says she does not consent to use of her face Emphasising that the use of her identity has not been authorised, Neha stated, “I DO NOT CONSENT TO THE UNAUTHORIZED USE OF MY FACE OR LIKENESS.”

The actor also warned those behind the creation or circulation of the content that she intends to pursue legal action. “Consider this a formal warning: I WILL TAKE LEGAL ACTION AGAINST EVERY INDIVIDUAL RESPONSIBLE FOR CREATING, POSTING, OR CIRCULATING SUCH CONTENT,” she wrote.

Addressing users who may believe that anonymous accounts or AI-generated material could shield them from accountability, Neha added, “No one should assume that hiding behind a fake account or the use of AI will protect them from accountability.” She ended the post with a direct message: “TAKE IT DOWN NOW. YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED.”

title: EXCLUSIVE: Frontal nudity gets censor clearance! CBFC retains 2-second adult magazine shot in Doosra; Abhinay Deo calls it an “achievement”
raw_summary:
The trailer of Doosra, which was recently unveiled, has caught attention for its unusual storytelling. The film not only revisits Sourav Ganguly's iconic moment following India's historic victory over England in the 2002 NatWest Series final but also follows the parallel story of Tara (Plabita Borthakur), a young girl growing up in a deeply conservative household in Rajasthan. While films of this nature are usually expected to receive a 'U' or 'U/A' certificate, Doosra has been granted an 'A' certificate by the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC). Interestingly, director Abhinay Deo willingly accepted the adult certification rather than agree to certain cuts. In an exclusive interview with Bollywood Hungama, the filmmaker revealed why he took this decision.

When asked about the certification Doosra received from the CBFC, Abhinay Deo said, "It’s an adult-rated movie due to a few scenes. I was there at the censor screening and they asked me, ‘What rating do you want?’. I suggested a U/A rating. They agreed but asked us to cut 3 scenes. I told them, ‘If we can get the film passed with an A-rating and without a cut, I won’t mind’. They said, ‘If you are okay with adult-rating, we won’t cut a single shot’. I agreed."

Abhinay Deo remarked, "It’s an achievement as nowadays, even films with ‘A’ have to go through cuts."

One of the scenes that contributed to the 'A' certification features Tara's father (Ankur Vikal) catching her with an adult magazine during her childhood. The sequence includes a clear, two-second shot of a nude photograph of a woman in the magazine. The CBFC has often been strict about the depiction of nudity on screen, with several films facing cuts over such content. However, in this case, the board allowed the shot to remain intact.

Abhinay Deo revealed, "Those 2-3 shots, which they wanted to cut, were integral to the film. One was the magazine shot. Then, we had a reference where we touched upon the Babri Masjid episode. They told me, ‘Thoda kam kar do, change kar do’. I confessed that I didn’t want to touch the film."

Was Abhinay Deo apprehensive about losing out on the under-18 audience because of the adult certification? He replied, "No, because this is not a film for teenagers to watch, though it is relevant to them."

Doosra is scheduled to release in cinemas on October 23.

Under his leadership, the department has cracked down on several restaurants and dark stores operated by quick-commerce companies over alleged violations of food safety and hygiene norms. The source continued, "As a result, in a rare instance, the multiplex continued functioning but without the option of selling snacks and beverages to patrons."

Interestingly, there were also reports that, owing to this extraordinary situation, the multiplex management allowed patrons to carry outside food, something that is otherwise generally restricted. However, Bollywood Hungama couldn't independently verify this information.

The source further revealed, "The F&B area of INOX R City Mall was sealed on October 9. It was only on October 13 that the theatre was once again allowed to sell food items." However, the source was unable to confirm the exact nature of the violations that prompted the FDA's action.

The incident is significant as food and beverage sales form an important revenue stream for multiplexes. It also comes at a time when the Maharashtra FDA, under Tukaram Mundhe, has intensified its inspections of food establishments across the state.

title: Akka teaser out: Netflix CONFIRMS October 30 premiere for Keerthy Suresh and Radhika Apte-starrer
raw_summary:
Netflix has unveiled the teaser of Akka, its upcoming series starring Keerthy Suresh and Radhika Apte. The teaser introduces the two actors as Bhavani and Rudra, respectively, in Pernuru, a kingdom shaped by traditions, rivalries and shifting power dynamics. The series is set to premiere on October 30, 2026.

The teaser was released on October 17 to coincide with Keerthy Suresh’s birthday. Produced by YRF Entertainment, Akka is described as a gangster saga centred on women and their influence in a world governed by its own rules.

Set in the 1980s, the series follows a fictional kingdom shaped by generations of women who have built, governed and protected Pernuru. Written and directed by Dharmaraj Shetty, Akka marks his directorial debut. The cast also includes Tanvi Azmi. Keerthy Suresh on playing Bhavani in Akka Speaking about the teaser release, Keerthy Suresh said, “The love I receive from the audience every year makes this day incredibly meaningful, and being able to celebrate it by unveiling the teaser of Akka, a project so close to my heart, feels truly special.”

Describing her character, the actor added, “Bhavani is one of the most unique and memorable characters I have had the opportunity to play. It was lovely working with Radhika. Our characters bring such compelling dynamics to the story and the interplay between them adds an intriguing edge to the narrative.”

Akka also marks Keerthy’s first series with Netflix and YRF Entertainment. Explaining what drew her to the project, she said, “What drew me to this project was the distinctiveness of its story and the world it inhabits. I am looking forward to audiences immersing themselves in this world and discovering the many facets of Bhavani as her story unfolds.” Radhika Apte talks about her character Rudra Radhika Apte, who plays Rudra, spoke about the character’s motivations and the story’s central conflicts. “Rudra is a fascinating character, driven by her own convictions and an instinct to challenge the world around her. What drew me to the series was the complexity of its characters and the tensions that emerge from their differing perspectives,” she said.

The actor also noted that the teaser and date announcement coinciding with Keerthy’s birthday made the occasion special. “It's wonderful that the date announcement and the teaser drop of Akka has coincided with Keerthy's birthday. I am sure it is going to be lucky for us,” she added.

Radhika, who has worked with Netflix on several projects, also spoke about collaborating with YRF Entertainment. “Collaborating with YRF Entertainment on a story with such layered characters has been a rewarding experience, and I look forward to audiences discovering Rudra and the many dimensions of her journey,” she said.

Akka premieres on Netflix on October 30, 2026.

title: Kriti Sanon approaches Delhi High Court seeking protection against AI-generated impersonation, unauthorised use of identity
raw_summary:
Bollywood actress Kriti Sanon has approached the Delhi High Court seeking protection of her personality and publicity rights against the alleged unauthorised use of her name, image, likeness and other aspects of her identity. Her plea also covers the alleged use of artificial intelligence (AI)-generated content and digital impersonation.

The matter came up before a single-judge Bench of Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav. During the hearing, the court asked Kriti's counsel to place on record relevant judgments, research papers and other material concerning the legal questions surrounding personality rights.

The High Court indicated that it would pass a comprehensive order after examining the judgments and research material submitted by the actress's legal team. The matter has now been listed for further hearing on October 29. Kriti Sanon seeks protection of her identity in the digital space Kriti's plea comes at a time when the unauthorised use of celebrities' identities through digital platforms has become an increasingly prominent legal issue. Apart from the unauthorised commercial use of names and images, courts are also dealing with cases involving AI-generated content, deepfakes, digital impersonation and fake endorsements.

Personality and publicity rights generally seek to protect aspects of an individual's identity from being commercially exploited or represented without authorisation. The growing use of generative AI has added another layer to these disputes, as digitally created images, videos and other content can closely imitate public figures.

The Delhi High Court has heard several cases in recent months involving celebrities and public figures seeking protection against such alleged misuse.

title: The best ending for Drishyam is NO Drishyam 4. Why Ajay Devgn and Abhishek Pathak are RIGHT to end the blockbuster franchise
raw_summary:
At a time when Bollywood is obsessed with franchises and cinematic universes, Drishyam: The Conclusion has proved that knowing when to end a successful story could be as important as knowing how to begin one.

The phenomenal success of Drishyam The Conclusion has once again demonstrated the extraordinary popularity of Ajay Devgn's Vijay Salgaonkar. Released on October 2, the suspense thriller has emerged as one of the biggest Bollywood successes of 2026, crossing the Rs. 500 crore mark at the worldwide box office. At a time when even star-studded entertainers are struggling to justify their budgets, Drishyam The Conclusion has proved that an engaging story, memorable characters and clever writing can still bring audiences to cinemas in huge numbers.

Going by conventional Bollywood logic, this should be the perfect opportunity to announce Drishyam 4. After all, why would any producer willingly discontinue a franchise capable of generating hundreds of crores?

Yet, director Abhishek Pathak has made it clear that the journey of Vijay Salgaonkar has reached its destination and that there are no plans for another instalment. It is a decision that deserves to be celebrated, not questioned. Because, sometimes, the smartest decision a filmmaker can make is to walk away from a goldmine. The Rs. 500 crore temptation

Let's face it. If Drishyam 4 were announced tomorrow, the trade would undoubtedly sit up and take notice. The combination of Ajay Devgn, Vijay Salgaonkar, October 2 and the promise of another mind-bending climax would be sufficient to generate enormous curiosity.

The producers already have something that filmmakers spend years trying to create: an established franchise with tremendous audience goodwill.

The first Drishyam (2015) gradually acquired a cult following, while Drishyam 2 (2022) emerged as a major theatrical success at a time when the Hindi film industry desperately needed reassurance that audiences were willing to return to cinemas. Drishyam The Conclusion has taken the franchise's commercial potential to an entirely different level.

Therefore, commercially speaking, making another instalment might appear to be a no-brainer.

But cinema cannot always be reduced to a balance sheet. There is a difference between a film making money because it has a compelling story and a film being made simply because there is money to be earned.

And that is precisely the trap which Drishyam must avoid.

The brilliance of Drishyam lies in its central premise. Vijay Salgaonkar is an ordinary family man blessed with extraordinary intelligence and an obsessive understanding of cinema. When his family faces an unimaginable crisis, he uses his knowledge, presence of mind and meticulous planning to protect his loved ones.

The character works because audiences identify with his circumstances, understand his desperation and are fascinated by his ability to remain several steps ahead of the investigating authorities.

But there is a limit to how many times the same formula can be repeated.

How many more investigations can Vijay outsmart? How many more officers can enter Goa determined to expose him? How many more times can audiences be asked to believe that the same family is caught in another elaborate cat-and-mouse game?

The first time, it was extraordinary. The second time, it was thrilling because the writers found an ingenious way to revisit the consequences of the original crime. The third film had the responsibility of bringing this remarkable journey to a satisfying conclusion.

A fourth instalment would face an even bigger challenge: justifying why a story that has already reached its conclusion needs to begin again.

There is also the danger of turning Vijay Salgaonkar into an almost superhuman figure. The character's greatest strength is that he is believable despite his extraordinary intelligence. If he continues to escape increasingly impossible circumstances, the franchise could eventually lose the very credibility that made it special.

Hindi cinema's growing dependence on established intellectual properties is understandable. Sequels offer brand recognition, relatively easier marketing and an audience already familiar with the characters.

But the success of a franchise should not automatically become a licence to extend it indefinitely.

Increasingly, Bollywood appears more interested in announcing the next instalment, spin-off or cinematic universe than allowing individual stories to breathe. Franchise-building is becoming an industrial strategy rather than a purely creative decision.

There is nothing inherently wrong with this approach. A well-written sequel can expand a fictional world and deliver an experience superior to its predecessor. However, the crucial question should always be whether the next film has a story worth telling.

Not whether the previous film collected Rs. 300 crores or Rs. 500 crores.

In that respect, the decision to conclude Drishyam is refreshing. It sends out a message that not every successful property needs to be exploited until audience enthusiasm disappears.

After all, the biggest threat to a beloved franchise is not necessarily a flop. Sometimes, it is one unnecessary sequel too many.

Sometimes, the best way to ensure that audiences remember a story forever is to resist the urge to keep telling it.

Drishyam has spent three films teaching us that Vijay Salgaonkar always knows how to stay one step ahead.

Perhaps the makers can take a lesson from their own protagonist and stay one step ahead of Bollywood's sequel obsession.

The audience may want Drishyam 4. The box office may justify Drishyam 4. But that doesn't mean Bollywood needs Drishyam 4.

title: Amit Trivedi makes a SHOCKING confession about Anurag Kashyap’s No Smoking: “Mujhe film dekh ke kuch samaj nahin aaya!”; reveals Shilpa Rao STRUGGLED to get him his Bollywood break
raw_summary:
Amit Trivedi spoke with Komal Nahta and revealed how he became a music composer. He began by saying, “I had done stage musical performances. Later, I worked in advertising for 4-5 years, as well as in television. I wanted to do something in the field of independent music, but working in films was never my aim. Also, mere family mein duur-duur tak films se koi naata nahin tha.”

He said, “While working in the field of advertising, I met Shilpa Rao. She used to sing a lot of ads in the studios regularly. I fell in love with her voice. Also, she was a wonderful person and we became close friends. One day, I expressed my wish of collaborating with her for an album. She agreed. The first song I made in collaboration with her was ‘Dhol Yaara Dhol’ (which later became a part in Dev D; 2009). I wanted to create its music video and then pitch it to MTV or Sony. However, she was very ambitious. She took this and other songs to film directors.”

When remarked that Shilpa Rao struggled on his behalf, Amit Trivedi guffawed and replied, “In a way, you can say that!”

He added, “One fine day, she called me and said, ‘I met Anurag Kashyap sir and I played some stuff. Tu aa ke milega kya?’. I replied, ‘Why are you doing this? We are thinking of a music album and going independent. Yeh film ki chakkar mein kahaan pad rahi hai yaar? This is not my scene’.  I was reluctant because I was inherently shy. The film world seemed very overwhelming and intimidating for me. I thought ki main apni choti si duniya mein main theek hoon! But Shilpa threw me into it and that’s how Anurag sir became the first personality whom I met.”

Amit Trivedi continued, “I had some apprehensions, but Anurag sir made me very comfortable. It was the time when Black Friday (2007) had just been released and work was going on for No Smoking (2007). He even showed us No Smoking. For the first time, I saw a raw version of a film without background score or dubbing. However, mujhe woh film dekh ke kuch samaj nahin aaya (laughs). I started wondering what I would tell him if he asked me, ‘Kaisi lagi film’!”

No Smoking starred John Abraham in the lead along with Paresh Rawal and Ranvir Shorey in the supporting cast.

title: Amit Trivedi reveals Dev D was initially put on HOLD: “Ronnie Screwvala was not keen on making it”; recalls how he TREMBLED before presenting songs to Anurag Kashyap: "I feared this would be the first and last film of my career!"
raw_summary:
Amit Trivedi had a conversation with Komal Nahta in which he revealed that he had no plans of composing songs for films. However, he made independent music with singer Shilpa Rao; the latter made Anurag Kashyap heard those songs and that’s how Anurag got interested to meet Amit Trivedi. This was a time when the acclaimed filmmaker was working on Dev D (2009), starring Abhay Deol.

Amit Trivedi said, “Anurag sir told me that he was doing a modern-day Devdas and that it had a requirement of some 12-15 songs. He shared some ideas and references. All this was very new for me. I went home and started working immediately. I took 6 months to compose 6 songs as my advertising work was also going on. 6 months later, Shilpa asked me for an update. I told her, ‘Are you sure you want to do this? Sir must have forgotten our meeting’. But she insisted that we had to meet him again.”

He continued, “Earlier, we met in Anurag sir’s office. This time, the meeting took place in my studio. Anurag sir came along with Vikas Bahl. Trust me, main kaanp raha tha. I was 26-27 years old. I had not seen Devdas. So, I saw both Dilip Kumar’s Devdas (1955) as well as Shah Rukh Khan’s Devdas (2002). That gave me an idea about the plot. Then, I composed as per what I understood. I feared ki main gaali khaunga and that this would be the first and last song of my career! However, they were so impressed and they liked all the songs.”

Amit added, “The next day, they called me for narration. I didn’t know what that meant (laughs). I heard the story after which I composed two more songs – ‘Saali Khushi’ and ‘Pardesi’. After listening to the tracks, Anurag sir tweaked a bit of the script and reimagined the film. I was like, ‘Wow. Aisa bhi hota hain’!”

He also stated, “Then, something happened. I don’t know exactly, but producer Ronnie Screwvala sir was not keen on making Dev D. So, the film went on hold. Anurag sir met me and said, ‘You have worked enough on Dev D. Tu abhi ruk jaa. Thoda hold pe hain. Meanwhile, I am producing a film called Aamir (2008). Raj Kumar Gupta is directing it. You work on this film while I figure out a way forward for Dev D’.”

Aamir, starring Rajeev Khandelwal, released first and hence marked Amit Trivedi’s debut as a film composer, even though Dev D was the first film he had worked on. Dev D eventually released eight months later.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Addinath M Kothare reveals 2 out of 5 ACs on Nayyi Navelli sets were reserved ONLY for him: “My sweat was dripping through the prosthetics; andar se mera body melt ho raha tha!”
raw_summary:
For many viewers, Addinath M Kothare has emerged as one of the biggest surprises in Nayyi Navelli. An unexpected twist in the story has made his character and performance stand out. In an exclusive interview with Bollywood Hungama, Addinath M Kothare spoke about the response to his role, the challenges of working on the film, his experience with Yami Gautam Dhar and a lot more.

How has the response to your character in Nayyi Navelli been? It's been amazing so far. I am quite overwhelmed with the response that I am getting for my character. It's a festive family entertainer, which has been aptly released during the festive season. Hence, it's lovely to be in this space right now.

The film has a Dussehra connection. Is that why the makers decided to release it during this festive period? Absolutely. This is also why they fast-tracked the entire shoot. It was a very difficult film to make due to the VFX, fantasy elements, ensemble cast, songs, etc. Yet, it was a very well-planned and efficiently executed project. We started shooting in April, and here we are. So, it's amazing!

It's a passionately made film. The kind of detailing that has gone into it and the efforts taken by the team deserve special mention. Ravi Srivastava, who has worked on films like Slumdog Millionaire (2008) and Lion (2016), handled the production design of our film. Rishi Punjabi's cinematography is phenomenal. The whole team worked really hard. As for Aanand L Rai sir and Himanshu Sharma, they are master storytellers, as we all know (smiles).

Horror-comedy has become quite popular now, but you and your family have been pioneers in this genre. Your father, Mahesh Kothare, made the cult film Zapatlela (1993), followed by Pachhadlela (2004), on which you worked as an assistant director. You also acted in Zapatlela 2 (2013). What are your thoughts on returning to this genre?

(Laughs) Quite honestly, you can't plan or even predict these things. I feel blessed that I got a film in this genre. I am also fortunate that two of my films are releasing quite close to each other. While Nayyi Navelli is a fantasy centred around mythology, Ramayana is a historical.

How was your experience of working with Yami Gautam Dhar? It was amazing. Despite being such a big star, she is very grounded and easy to talk to. She was also extremely helpful.

When you begin working on a film, you are still searching for your character, his body language, etc. Moreover, the film is set in Meerut, and I had to work a lot on the dialect, as I was the only non-North Indian actor on the set! Thankfully, I was somewhat familiar with the accent because of the films we watch. So, it wasn't completely alien to me. Also, in Mumbai, you get to hear the UP accent quite often.

Nevertheless, I had to work a lot on the dialect and other aspects of the character. On my first or second day of the shoot, Yami, Balaji Mohan sir and I were having a conversation. Yami cracked a joke, and I laughed. As I laughed, she stared at me for a moment and said, "Adi, this is Raja!" At that point, I was still trying to find the character. I knew I was close, but her observation helped push me in the right direction.

You had to wear extensive prosthetics, and a lot of VFX was also used for your scenes. How challenging was the experience? That was the biggest challenge of the film. I was covered in prosthetics from head to toe. There were prosthetic patches on my face, including my forehead and the veins on my face and neck. From my neck to my toes, I was wearing a complete silicone prosthetic bodysuit. There were days when I had to wear it for 12 hours!

It used to take me four hours to get ready and another one-and-a-half hour to remove the prosthetics. Moreover, we were shooting in May! But the production and direction teams took great care of me. On the sets, we had these anaconda ACs. They consisted of an AC unit with huge tubes that would crawl all over the set, just like anaconda snakes. There were five such ACs in total. Whenever I wore the suit, two of those five anacondas were reserved exclusively for me (laughs)!

I remember that on the first and second days, I became so itchy that I simply couldn't bear it. Thankfully, the direction team asked me to take a break. I got out of the suit, and we began figuring out how to get rid of the itchiness and make it possible for me to wear the suit for longer durations. Slowly, through trial and error, we found a solution. Before putting on the suit, I would cover myself with Abzorb Dusting Powder. There would be a thick layer of powder, almost 2 cm, all over my body! On top of that, I would wear a sweatsuit, like the ones swimmers wear, and then the prosthetics. That made things easier, though it took us two days to figure it out.

Yet, there were challenges. One day, I was wearing the prosthetics and rehearsing with Yami. Suddenly, I noticed that the floor had become wet. I wondered, ‘Yeh paani kahan se aa raha hai?’ Then I realized that my sweat was dripping through the silicone prosthetics! Andar se mera body melt ho raha tha!

How many days did you have to shoot wearing the prosthetics? We shot for around 50 days, out of which I wore the prosthetics for 20 days. I had to perform and get the emotions right while wearing that suit. Hence, it was a physically and mentally challenging process. But the production team was well-equipped to ensure that the actors were comfortable despite these challenges. That's the only reason I could pull it off.
